heading: EXT. DRY WASH - HIGH DESERT - DAWN

units.text: EXT. DRY WASH - HIGH DESERT - DAWN
A dry riverbed.
Sage, cracked clay, a lone cottonwood bleached white.
A horse stands hobbled by the tree, nosing at the dust.
A campfire has burned to a gray nest.
A RIDER, fifties, hat low, sits on a flat stone with a tin cup.
A graying beard.
A slow way of moving, as if he'd spent a lifetime bargaining with his joints.
He tilts the cup.
Dregs.
He tosses them on the ashes.
Don't look at me like that. It's the last of the coffee.
units.name: RIDER

units.text: The horse flicks an ear.
He reaches into his saddlebag and withdraws a folded sheet of paper, brown at the creases.
Smooths it on his knee.
Reads in silence.
Then, aloud:
"Dear Abel. The farm is sold. Your sister has the boy. Do not come back, for there is nothing to come back to."
units.name: RIDER

units.text: He lowers the letter.
The wind lifts the edge of it.
He holds it down with a thumb.
Abel Corrigan. That's me. You never asked.
units.name: RIDER

units.text: The horse snorts.
Well. Now you know.
units.name: ABEL

units.text: He folds the letter along its creases and tucks it into his hatband.
He gets to his feet in stages.
Forty miles to the river.
units.name: ABEL

units.text: From somewhere a long way off, down the wash, comes the thin whistle of a train.
Would you listen to that.
units.name: ABEL

units.text: He takes the horse's reins.
He leads it a few paces, stops, and stands listening until the whistle fades.
"Dear Father. We are well. The boy has your eyes."
units.name: ABEL

units.text: Hush now.
units.name: ABEL

units.text: He mounts, slowly, and rides out along the wash toward the east, where the sun has begun to lift itself over the ridge.
